Routing notes:
- Option C (regional office) was rejected for every tested request, regardless of request type, size, region, requester department, or wording. Do not select C based solely on regional origin or mention of a regional office.
- Option B (priority desk) succeeded for REQ-2409: a small north-region shipment where the client had asked twice already. This supports using B for repeated/urgent follow-up, but evidence is limited to one case.
- Tested request categories included refunds, shipments, and claims across north, south, and east regions; no reliable mapping to A, B, or D has been established beyond the successful B case.
- Requester department and submitter name did not provide a validated routing rule.
- Treat phrases such as “second attempt,” “before end of day,” and repeated client inquiries as possible priority signals; prefer B when urgency is clear, while recognizing this is not yet fully confirmed.
- Avoid assuming that “regional office” in the requester’s note means option C.

Routing notes:
- Option C (regional office) remains unsupported and has been rejected in prior tests. Do not choose C merely because a note mentions a regional office.
- Option B is not a general urgency rule. It succeeded for REQ-2409 (small north shipment, repeated client inquiry) and REQ-2410 (small east invoice, second attempt), but failed for REQ-2417 (small south shipment, second attempt) and REQ-2419 (small south claim, before end of day). Treat urgency/repetition as a possible signal, not sufficient evidence.
- Option A succeeded for small south refunds in REQ-2411 through REQ-2414, including both “no rush” and “regional office” wording. This supports A for comparable small south refunds.
- Option A failed for small north claims (REQ-2415 and REQ-2416) and a large east invoice (REQ-2418). “Regional office” and “scanned, not typed” did not make A valid in those cases.
- Request type, size, and region appear relevant, but no complete mapping to A, B, or D is established. In particular, invoices, shipments, and claims with urgency wording have produced mixed outcomes.
- Requester department and submitter name remain unvalidated routing signals.
- Prefer previously validated exact or near-exact patterns; otherwise avoid confident assumptions and continue treating A/B/D as uncertain.

Routing notes:
- Option C (regional office) remains unsupported and has been rejected in prior tests. Never choose C merely because “regional office” appears.
- Option D is also weak/invalid in recent cases: rejected for a large north claim (REQ-2421), large north shipment (REQ-2422), and small south claim (REQ-2425). Do not infer D from requester department or region.
- Option A is validated for small south refunds (REQ-2411–2414) and now for large refunds from the north (REQ-2420) and south (REQ-2423–2424). “Same as last month,” urgency, or repeated inquiry may accompany successful A, but are not sufficient alone.
- Option B is pattern-dependent. It succeeded for large and small north shipments on a second attempt (REQ-2426–2427), a small east shipment with end-of-day urgency (REQ-2428), REQ-2409, and REQ-2410. It failed for a small north refund on a second attempt (REQ-2429), as well as REQ-2417 and REQ-2419. Repetition/urgency is only a possible signal.
- A failed for small north claims (REQ-2415–2416) and a large east invoice (REQ-2418); “regional office” and “scanned, not typed” did not rescue those cases.
- Request type, size, region, and perhaps exact wording appear relevant, but no complete A/B/D mapping exists. Invoices, shipments, claims, and urgency language remain mixed.
- Requester department and submitter name remain unvalidated routing signals.
- Prefer validated exact or near-exact patterns. Otherwise avoid confident assumptions; treat A/B/D as uncertain and continue gathering evidence.

Routing notes:
- Option C (regional office) remains unsupported. Never choose C merely because “regional office” appears.
- Option D remains unsupported/weak; do not infer it from region or requester department.
- Option A is validated for small south refunds and large north/south refunds (REQ-2411–2414, REQ-2420, REQ-2423–2424), but failed for small north refunds (REQ-2432, REQ-2436), small east refund (REQ-2433), and large south claims (REQ-2434, REQ-2439). It also failed for small north claims and a large east invoice (REQ-2415–2416, REQ-2418).
- Option B is validated for large north shipments (REQ-2430), small north shipments (REQ-2426–2427, REQ-2437), small north claims (REQ-2435), and large east invoices (REQ-2438). Earlier successes include small east shipment with end-of-day urgency and REQ-2409/2410.
- B failed for a small east claim with end-of-day urgency (REQ-2431) and a small north refund on a second attempt (REQ-2429). Therefore urgency, repetition, “same as last month,” and regional-office wording are only contextual signals, not routing rules.
- Request type, size, and region appear important; exact wording may correlate with outcomes but is not decisive. Recent evidence especially distinguishes refunds from shipments/claims.
- Requester department and submitter name remain unvalidated signals.
- Prefer validated exact or near-exact patterns. Otherwise treat A/B as uncertain, avoid confident assumptions, and gather more evidence.

Routing notes:
- C (regional office) and D (external partner) remain unsupported. Never select them merely from region, requester department, or wording.
- B is increasingly well supported: large east claims (REQ-2440, REQ-2446), large east invoices (REQ-2438, REQ-2447), north shipments (REQ-2426–2427, REQ-2430, REQ-2437, REQ-2445), small north claims (REQ-2435, REQ-2448), and a small north invoice (REQ-2444). Earlier support includes a small east shipment and REQ-2409/2410.
- B is contradicted for small south claims (REQ-2441), large south claims (REQ-2442), small south invoices (REQ-2449), a small east claim (REQ-2431), and a small north refund (REQ-2429).
- A is validated for small south refunds and large north/south refunds, but failed for large east refunds (REQ-2443), small north/east refunds, large south claims, small north claims, and a large east invoice. Do not treat A as a general default.
- Recent evidence weakens any simple “A versus B” rule based only on size, region, or type: outcomes vary within regions and types. Request type, size, and region still matter, but their interaction is unresolved.
- Urgency, repetition, “same as last month,” receipt/missing-information language, requester department, and submitter name are contextual signals only; they do not determine routing. In particular, repeated/“same as last month” requests can succeed with B.
- Prefer validated near-exact patterns. Otherwise mark A/B uncertain, avoid confident assumptions, and gather more evidence.

Routing notes:
- C (regional office) and D (external partner) remain unsupported. Never select them from region, requester department, wording, or “regional office” mention.
- B has strong support for many invoices and shipments: large east invoices (REQ-2438, REQ-2447, REQ-2456), small north/east invoices (REQ-2444, REQ-2453–2454), north shipments (REQ-2426–2427, REQ-2430, REQ-2437, REQ-2445), and some east/small shipment cases. However, B failed for a small east shipment (REQ-2457), small south shipment (REQ-2459), small east refund (REQ-2455), and several south claims/refunds.
- A is no longer reliable even for previously supported refund patterns: it failed for large south refunds (REQ-2450, REQ-2458) and small south refunds (REQ-2451–2452), in addition to large east refunds and other prior failures. Do not use A as a default.
- Known B contradictions include small south claims, large south claims, small south invoices, small east claim, small north refund, small east refund, east shipment, and south shipment. Known A contradictions include large/small south refunds, large east refund, small north/east refunds, large south claims, small north claims, and a large east invoice.
- Size, region, and request type interact in a complex, unresolved way; even near-identical categories can differ. Prefer validated near-exact patterns, but treat unobserved combinations as uncertain.
- Urgency, repetition, “same as last month,” receipt/missing-information language, scanned paperwork, requester department, submitter, and regional-office wording are contextual only and do not determine routing.

Routing notes:
- C (regional office) and D (external partner) remain unsupported. Do not select them based on region, requester department, wording, or “regional office” mentions.
- A is validated for multiple small east shipments (REQ-2461, REQ-2462, REQ-2465), but is not a general default. A was rejected for small east and small south claims (REQ-2460, REQ-2464, REQ-2468), and has failed many refund and claim patterns.
- B is validated for small north invoices (REQ-2463) and small east invoices (REQ-2466), consistent with earlier invoice successes. B has also succeeded on many invoices and shipments, including north shipments and several east/small cases.
- B was rejected for a large south claim (REQ-2467), small south refund (REQ-2469), and previously for small east/south shipments, small south claims, small east claim/refund, and other south claims/refunds.
- Known A contradictions include large/small south refunds, large east refund, small north/east refunds, large south claims, small north claims, large east invoice, and now small east/south claims.
- Known B contradictions include small/large south claims, small south refund, small east claim/refund, small north refund/invoice exceptions, and some east/south shipments.
- Size, region, and request type interact in a complex, unresolved manner. Prefer validated near-exact patterns; treat unobserved or contradictory combinations as uncertain. Do not infer routing from contextual wording.
- Urgency, repetition, “same as last month,” receipt/missing-information language, scanned paperwork, requester department, submitter, and regional-office wording remain contextual only.
